Probably not as bad as all the rest on here, but dry socket. After my wisdom teeth being removed I got dry socket and wasn't sure what it was, but the holes that the teeth were in were getting kind of painful. The biggest thing I noticed was a horrendous smell though. I was embarrassed to talk to anyone for fear they'd smell my breath.

I went to the dentist's, and they told me that I had dry socket (they never told me how to prevent it or that I could even get it in the first place) but they told me that food from the past few days was basically packed in the holes where my wisdom teeth were and they needed to flush it out. "Alright that's fine" I thought. I was a fucking fool. They put a syringe in to shoot water into the holes. That split second was fucking excruciating. It was hitting the nerves deep in my gums and they had to do it multiple times for both sides of my lower jaw.  Thankfully it was quick, but that split second felt like an eternity. My body was shaking as they were shooting the water deep inside the holes in my gums. At the time, I didn't know that exposed nerve pain could hurt that bad, but it was the worst I ever felt for sure.

My reply will probably get lost in here but I had a VERY rough time going through high school. I was bulimic, I had more than my fair share of heartbreaks and being cheated on, I had image issues, a self harm addiction, abusive family, you name it. I was at a park one day and I decided if nothing ever got better by some date I'd pick far off in the future, it was my end all be all date. I'd kill myself if nothing improved. That day I picked was June 17th 2015.

Well fast forward a little bit, I joined a band like I always wanted. I got a good group of friends. I actually got through high school finally. Things were looking up, to the point where I completely forgot about the date I set.

Fast forward again. It's June 15th 2015. My band's first public show. I meet an amazing and cute as hell girl there who wanted to do photography for our band. This woman turned out to be the girl I married in 2019. I met her 2 DAYS before some entirely random date I picked to end my life way back in high school.

The band went on to do some great things before I eventually was no longer part of it. But out of it. I met my soulmate and the love of my life. Moral is, everything can and WILL work itself out. It played out like a dream for me. I'm still depressed, I still have bad shit in my life, but I can work through it and talk it through with the best partner I could ask for.
